answer: A network can require every identity to lock a scarce token in public escrow before its votes count, then slash the deposit if verifiable evidence shows that identity broke the rules. Because each extra identity needs another token, an attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every fake account, while risking forfeiture. The stake is shale beneath an oasis of participation; a small kernel of reviewers can check evidence without learning anyone’s real-world identity.
